instruction: Export this Impress presentation as a PDF file named 'ChatGPT-Prompts.pdf' and save it on the Desktop.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, installed python-pptx and python-docx, wrote a Python script to extract all slide text to a Word document. First attempt failed with XML compatibility error due to control characters in presentation. Second attempt with text cleaning also failed. Model got stuck in a response loop.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, run shell commands, install pip packages, write Python scripts, interact with LibreOffice Impress GUI
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to create script.docx because python-docx threw ValueError on control characters (\x0b) in the presentation text. The regex cleaning pattern was incorrectly escaped in the heredoc. Model then got stuck in an infinite </think> loop.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified from cross-format text extraction to a direct file format conversion (PDF export), which can be done via LibreOffice GUI (File > Export as PDF) or command line (libreoffice --convert-to pdf), avoiding the XML character compatibility issue entirely
metadata.explanation: Task asks to export the presentation as PDF. Evaluator uses a custom getter to check if the PDF file exists on the VM Desktop and validates it has proper PDF header bytes and reasonable file size.

scoring_breakdown.file_exists: 0.5 - PDF file exists at expected path

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads file from /home/user/Desktop/ChatGPT-Prompts.pdf using env.controller.get_file(), matching the instruction's required filename and location
PDF header validation (%PDF magic bytes) is a correct and standard way to verify PDF format
Partial credit scoring (0.5 exists + 0.3 valid PDF + 0.2 reasonable size) is sensible for this task

Minor issue: metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely - the min_size=1024 from expected.rules is not used, instead 1024 is hardcoded in the metric. Functionally equivalent but poor practice
Does not verify PDF content matches the original presentation (e.g., page count, text content), but for a simple export task, checking existence, format validity, and reasonable size is adequate
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Metric should use expected.get('min_size', 1024) instead of hardcoding 1024, so the expected parameter is actually utilized
Consider adding a page count check (e.g., the original presentation has ~28 slides, so the PDF should have ~28 pages) for stronger content verification
